title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 'loop equation' study (sequel to La Longue Marche, around GT-type relations). An element xi of pi^_{0,3} (the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus 3 points) must satisfy an equation (68)/(93) involving an automorphism rho. Rho is induced by an element of order 3 acting on the profinite completion SL(2,Z^)'. The equation also involves a multiplier p = chi(u) = 2r+1 in Z^*, a cyclotomic-type character value.

On the previous page Grothendieck finds that, modulo the commutator, xi is either a 'twisted coboundary' xi = lambda rho(lambda)^{-1} or the other class xi = lambda' l0^{-1} rho(lambda')^{-1}. In nonabelian-cohomology language these are the two classes of 1-cocycles for the order-3 action.

Case A (previous page). D = delta(c^2+cd+d^2) and pD = 1. Since c^2+cd+d^2 takes only the values 0 and 1 mod 3, and D must be a unit, one gets p ≡ delta mod 3, where delta = det lambda is ±1.

This page:
- Case summary. xi = lambda rho(lambda)^{-1} with lambda in SL2 holds iff p ≡ 1 (3), iff r ≡ 0 (3). The twisted case holds iff p ≡ -1 (3), iff r ≡ -1 (3).
- Case B. Write lambda' = (a b; c d) with ad-bc = 1, l0^{-1} = (1 2; 0 1), and rho(lambda')^{-1} = (a-c, c; a+b-c-d, c+d), which also has determinant 1. Their product gives (99):
  - A = 3a^2+3ab+b^2-3ac-2ad-bc-bd
  - B = 3ac+2ad+bc+bd
  - D = 3c^2+3cd+d^2
  - C = -D + 3ac+ad+2bc+bd (my own computation).
- Hence C - B = -(ad-bc) - D = -1 - D, i.e. C + D - B = -1 (the margin NB).
- The defining equation (93) then reads 2rD = -1 - D, i.e. (100): (2r+1)D = -1, i.e. pD = -1. So (101): p = -1/D, where D is the lower-right entry of the image of xi in SL(2,Z^)'. The sign ambiguity is removed by the choice of lambda.

The next page completes the argument. D = 3c^2+3cd+d^2 ≡ d^2 mod 3 takes only the values 0 and 1, and D is a unit, so p ≡ -1 (3). Thus the cocycle class is detected by chi(u) mod 3.

Both quadratic forms have discriminant -3. With d' = d+c one gets 3c^2+3cd+d^2 = d'^2 + d'c + c^2, so both are the norm form of the Eisenstein integers. The upshot: the multiplier p is ±1 over a norm from Z^[omega]. This is a routine but tidy computation of how the cyclotomic parameter is constrained modulo the commutator subgroup.
errors: The written relation 'B - C = -1 + D' is inconsistent with (99) and det = 1. Direct computation gives B - C = (ad-bc) + D = 1 + D, i.e. C - B = -1 - D. That is what is actually needed to reach 2rD = -1 - D, and it matches the margin 'C + D - B = ...'. The line is heavily overwritten, so this may be a slip in writing rather than in reasoning; the boxed result pD = -1 is consistent.
The entry C in (99) is partly illegible. Recomputing gives C = -(3c^2+3cd+d^2) + 3ac + ad + 2bc + bd; the machine transcription has 2ad and bc in place of ad and 2bc.

On the next page Grothendieck corrects the second-case form to -(c^2+cd+d^2) in his remark. This is equivalent to 3c^2+3cd+d^2 up to change of variables and sign conventions, so it is not an error, but the normalisations differ between the two pages.

ideas.what: Splitting solutions xi of the loop equation into the two classes lambda rho(lambda)^{-1} vs lambda l0^{-1} rho(lambda)^{-1} (twisted conjugacy / nonabelian H^1 of an order-3 action), and detecting the class by the multiplier p mod 3
ideas.modern_name: nonabelian cohomology of Z/3 acting on SL2(Z^); constraints on GT elements from the order-3 relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; for SL2-level analyses of GT^, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the role of the order-2 and order-3 relations; this explicit computation is unpublished

ideas.what: Formula p = ±1/D, with D an Eisenstein norm form (c^2+cd+d^2 or 3c^2+3cd+d^2) in the entries of lambda, so p ≡ ±1 mod 3 accordingly
ideas.modern_name: cyclotomic character value expressed as a norm from Z^[omega] (CM torus centralizing the order-3 element)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; implicit in analyses of the image of GT^ in Aut(SL2(Z^)) and of the order-3 relation

missed.claim: Explicit SL2(Z^)-level reduction of the order-3 'loop equation': the multiplier is ±1 over an Eisenstein norm in the entries of lambda, and the twisted-conjugacy class of xi is detected by p mod 3. This is a small unpublished computation, essentially routine; its content is likely implicit in later studies of GT^ acting on SL2(Z^).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It documents that Grothendieck analysed the order-3 GT relation modulo commutators via norm forms of Z[omega]. This is of historical interest, not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine matrix computation within Grothendieck's unpublished study of the loop equation. The Eisenstein-norm observation is natural, and the mod-3 dichotomy is elementary.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 of the case summary reads 'p ≡ 1 (3) ⟺ r ≡ 0 (3)', not '3 | r [?]'.
Bottom-left page number '115'; the next page carries Grothendieck's own number 348.
Entry C in (99) is better read as C = -(3c^2+3cd+d^2) + 3ac + ad + 2bc + bd, per recomputation.
The margin 'NB C+D-B = ...' likely reads C + D - B = -(ad-bc) = -1.
Read 'rho' for 'g' in 'xi = lambda rho(lambda)^{-1}' throughout; l0 is the matrix (1 2; 0 1) up to inverse.
